messages:
Marie Chen: Quick check-in on the interface encapsulation spike from last RFC. Proposal: extract a thin 'session-core' service owning session lifecycle + KV cache APIs, keep request-router as thin proxy. Goal: reduce coupling and make per-tenant rollout easier. TL;DR: minimal public surface, compatibility shim for old clients for 90 days.

Alex Kim: What's the contract shape? request/response? Are we moving auth? :eyes:

Marie Chen: Contract is simple JSON over HTTP for now: Session {id, tenant, ttl, kv_prefix}. gRPC option later. Auth stays at the edge — tokens validated there. We'll add an internal header X-Session-Owner for routing.

Sanjay Patel: Concern: KV cache locality — moving ownership will change hot-path latency. Need microbenchmarks + p99 targets before any traffic flip. Can we keep a local LRU layer + remote authoritative store? Also need guidance on cross-service transactions (we should avoid sync cross-writes).

Devin Ortiz: For cutover, propose phased approach: 
1) New service reads from authoritative store but writes proxied to old service (dual-write).
2) Switch reads for a small percent of tenants.
3) Gradually increase traffic, flip writes when stable.
Canary windows: 48h, rollback path is to turn off canary flag.

Marie Chen: +1. Feature flag per-tenant will be required. Owners: @Marie Chen (lead), @Sanjay (perf), @Devin (cutover/runbook). I'll own the interface proto.

Kate Bot: ARCH-4523 created: "session-core perf bench + canary runbook". Assignee: Marie Chen.

Alex Kim: Tests: integration tests + chaos tests to simulate cache miss storms and partial failures. Need a migration plan for stale KV prefixes — add an epoch to the prefix so old keys don't collide.

Marie Chen: Example shim config we can reuse in the proxy:
```json
{"session_prefix": "v2-{{tenant}}-{{epoch}}", "compat_window_days": 90}
```
This lets us read both prefixes during the compatibility window.

Devin Ortiz: Ops checklist: dashboards for session_create latency (p50/p95/p99), cache hit ratio, error rate, and overall success rate. Add alert if error rate > 0.5% for 15m or if p99 latency regresses by >30%.

Sanjay Patel: Also add rollout metric: percent of tenants on v2 by org_id and a slow-start ramp plan (5%, 20%, 50%, 100%).

Alex Kim: Security note: validate X-Session-Owner at the edge. Consider signing the header with an internal key to prevent spoofing. Also run a token replay check during canary.

Marie Chen: Next steps: I'll draft the playbook and PR the interface proto + the compatibility shim by EOD Friday. Aim to start the spike next sprint (Mon). Action items in the ARCH ticket. :thumbsup:

Devin Ortiz: Sounds good. One more: storage/schema changes — prefer avoiding schema migration in this phase. Keep all migrations backwards-compatible.

Marie Chen: ✅ I’ll avoid schema work in phase 1 and document the follow-up if we need compaction later.

Alex Kim: If perf looks bad, fallback is to keep read path in router and only move write semantics. Let's keep that as plan B.

Sanjay Patel: I'll start a microbench harness this week and post numbers in the ticket.

Marie Chen: Thanks all — will post the RFC follow-up with concrete APIs and timeline in ARCH-4523.
